verdict.rationale: kitty's first-party remote-control docs describe controlling the terminal from scripts or the shell: opening new windows, sending arbitrary text input to any window, and changing titles, alongside programmable tabs, splits and layouts. Remote-control sockets are even forwarded over the ssh kitten, so the core of an agent creating panes and running commands through a documented interface is covered. missing for 10: explicit evidence of reading window output or scrollback via the control interface, detail on the protocol's wire format or security model, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven use.
